advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh to MCP_PATHS in autodeploy.sh so a change to the shared ensure script rebuilds the mcp image.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:140 `BOT_PATHS='... infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh'` — the script IS a review-bot rebuild trigger
autodeploy.sh:152 `MCP_PATHS='src/rebar infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp infra/compose/docker-compose.yml uv.lock pyproject.toml'` — omits infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh
Dockerfile.mcp:99 entrypoint runs `sh /app/infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` — the mcp image now functionally depends on that script, baked via `COPY . /app` (Dockerfile.mcp:42)
advisory.finding: autodeploy MCP_PATHS does not include infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh, though the mcp entrypoint now bakes (COPY . /app) and invokes that script — a change to the shared script rebuilds the review-bot but not the mcp image, so a fix to it silently never reaches the mcp container.
scenarios: A bug fix lands in reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh only; the mcp target sees no matching path change, skips its blue-green rebuild, and keeps running the old baked script indefinitely

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Set REBAR_SYNC_PUSH explicitly on the mcp service (both docker-compose.yml and mcp_run_new) to make the auto-push policy explicit and drift-proof, matching the reviewbot/opcert precedent.
evidence: docker-compose.yml:367-368 comment: 'URL-scoped git credential helper for the clone + auto-push'
docker-compose.yml:120 reviewbot sets `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: "always"` explicitly
docker-compose.yml:293 opcert sets `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: "off"` explicitly
ABSENCE: no REBAR_SYNC_PUSH key in the mcp service environment block (docker-compose.yml:333-371) nor in mcp_run_new (autodeploy.sh:346-371)
src/rebar/_store/push.py:4 default policy is `always`
advisory.finding: The mcp service relies on auto-push to the `tickets` branch (comments say '+auto-push') but never sets REBAR_SYNC_PUSH, silently inheriting the default `always`; the sibling reviewbot service sets `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: "always"` explicitly and opcert sets `off`, so the mcp service is the only pushing store whose push policy is implicit.
scenarios: A future change to the rebar default push policy silently disables mcp ticket-event persistence
An operator auditing which services push to the shared branch cannot tell from the mcp service definition
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: "always"` to the mcp service environment and a matching `-e REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always` in autodeploy.sh mcp_run_new.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the Dockerfile.mcp comment: the credential helper is written with `git config --global` and is URL-scoped by its config key, not repo-local scoped.
evidence: Dockerfile.mcp:70 `#   1. Configure a PER-URL (not --global) git credential helper`
Dockerfile.mcp:88 `echo '  git config --global "credential.${MCP_TICKETS_URL}.helper" \';`
Dockerfile.reviewbot:150 uses the identical `git config --global` while its comment (line 135) also says 'PER-URL (not --global)'
advisory.finding: The Dockerfile.mcp comment claims a 'PER-URL (not --global)' credential helper, but the generated entrypoint writes the helper with `git config --global` (a global-scope config, keyed per-URL) — the comment's parenthetical is factually wrong and mirrors the same misstatement in Dockerfile.reviewbot.
scenarios: A reader trusts the comment and assumes the helper is scoped to a repo-local config

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_0=safe.directory/VALUE_0=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets to the mcp compose service (and the -e equivalents in autodeploy's mcp_run_new), mirroring the review-bot fix.
evidence: compose-up.sh:170 `chown -R "${GERRIT_UID}:${GERRIT_UID}" "${SITE_HOST_DIR}"` chowns the whole /var/gerrit/site (incl. mcp-tickets) to uid 1000; SITE_SUBDIRS now includes `mcp-tickets` (compose-up.sh:30)
Dockerfile.mcp has no `USER` directive (search for USER returned no matches), so the mcp container runs as root over a uid-1000 volume — the exact situation the review-bot documents

docker-compose.yml:130-141 for review-bot: 'without safe.directory ... git's dubious-ownership guard (>=2.35.2) refused EVERY op on it — the ensure-tickets convergence AND rebar's runtime `git commit` ... making 100% of code_review artifact emissions fail'; it injects GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_0=safe.directory/VALUE_0
tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:2077-2092 pins that fix for review-bot; the new mcp service env (docker-compose.yml:361-392) sets REBAR_TRACKER_DIR + the volume but no GIT_CONFIG_* safe.directory
blocking.finding: The mcp compose service mounts the uid-1000-owned persistent tickets volume but omits the git safe.directory config the review-bot needs; git's dubious-ownership guard will refuse the clone, the ensure-registry convergence, and every runtime tool write.
scenarios: First deploy with a valid MCP_TICKETS_PAT: `git clone` into /var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets runs as root against a uid-1000 dir and is refused for dubious ownership
After any successful clone, reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh `git -C "$DIR" config`/fetch and rebar's runtime tool writes are all refused the same way
blocking.suggested_fix: In docker-compose.yml mcp `environment`, add GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: "1", GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: "safe.directory", GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: "/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets"; add the matching `-e` flags to mcp_run_new in autodeploy.sh and extend the parity test.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the blue-green 2x-overlap (two mcp containers on one gerrit_mcp_tickets volume + one tickets branch) with the commit's single-writer rationale — confirm the store write-lock and REBAR_SYNC_PUSH policy are safe under concurrent old+new writers, or scope pushes to a single writer.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:676 `# 4. start the NEW container ALONGSIDE the old.`
autodeploy.sh:369 `-v "gerrit_mcp_tickets:/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets"`
docker-compose.yml:392 `- gerrit_mcp_tickets:/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`
autodeploy.sh:707 old backend is only retired at step 7, after the new one is live — so both mount the same volume between steps 4 and 7

Commit message: 'the write lock would serialize two writers, but that store was provisioned for one and nothing in its design anticipates a second' — yet the blue-green overlap introduces exactly a second writer on the same volume + remote branch
dropped.finding: During a blue-green mcp deploy the new and old containers run simultaneously (2x overlap) and BOTH bind-mount `gerrit_mcp_tickets` and push to the same remote `tickets` branch, so the store has two concurrent writers — precisely the two-writer scenario the commit message says the dedicated volume was created to avoid.
scenarios: A blue-green mcp redeploy while the retiring container is still finishing an in-flight certified op that writes/pushes ticket events
Two containers racing the rebar write-lock / git push to origin/tickets
